newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Britain stage hostage wargame.
newsitem.headline: France, Britain stage hostage wargame.

text.p: France and Britain staged a hostage-freeing wargame on Wednesday, the first joint exercise for a Franco-British air command formed last year, officials said.

The so-called "Volcano" exercise, based on an attempt to free military commanders of the two countries held hostage by an enemy power, was to test and strengthen cooperation between the two countries.

The exercise, running from Tuesday to Thursday, was held in Chaumont and Damblain in eastern France. The British embassy said in a statement that a second joint exercise would be held in Britain in 1997.
The exercise involves about 30 planes, including French Mirages and British Tornados, refuelling aircraft, surveillance planes and heavy transport planes, along with more than 200 commandos.
French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major inaugurated the so-called "Franco-British Euro Air Group" last year at its base in High Wycombe west of London.

The small unit is to plan and command joint humanitarian operations in cases where it makes sense for the two European Union partners to work together -- for example in flying men and equipment to former Yugoslavia.
